title: Present perfect
point: Use have + past participle for life experience, something just finished, or a state that started in the past and continues now.

sentences.ja: 沖縄に行ったことある？
sentences.text: Have you ever been to Okinawa?
sentences.note: For visits, use "been to", not "gone to".

sentences.ja: 納豆は一回も食べたことがない。

sentences.note: "Have lunch" is more natural than "eat lunch" in this question.

sentences.ja: ちょうど課題を提出したところ。
sentences.text: I've just turned in my assignment.

sentences.note: The present perfect tells the listener the keys are still missing.

sentences.ja: ここに住んで五年になります。
sentences.text: I've lived here for five years.

sentences.ja: 月曜からずっと風邪気味なんだ。
sentences.text: I've had a cold since Monday.
sentences.note: English says you "have" a cold, so "have had" covers the whole stretch.

sentences.text: Long time no see! How have you been?

sentences.ja: まだその論文読んでないんだ。
sentences.text: I haven't read that paper yet.

sentences.ja: 彼女とは高校時代からの知り合いです。
sentences.text: I've known her since high school.
